title: Por vs. para
invitation: Want a quick lesson on why Spanish uses por or para here?
summary: Both words can correspond to English words such as “for,” but Spanish chooses between them according to the relationship being expressed. Learn the relationship, not an English one-word translation.

blocks.text: Instead of memorizing one English translation, notice what the phrase is doing: showing a path or reason, expressing a purpose or destination, naming a beneficiary, setting a deadline, and so on.
Use por for a path, route, or area something moves through or along.
Use por when the phrase gives a cause, reason, or motivation.
Por qué asks for a reason. Treat the whole interrogative expression as a unit rather than swapping por and para mechanically.
Por eso links a prior reason to its consequence: roughly ‘because of that’ or ‘therefore,’ depending on context.
Use por for a means, method, route, channel, or medium in many common constructions.
Use por in many exchange, price, replacement, and substitution relationships.
Por appears in distributive patterns such as uno por uno: one by one.
Use para to point toward an intended purpose or goal. Para + infinitive is a common way to express what something is done in order to accomplish.
Use para to point toward a destination, endpoint, or goal.
Use para to identify an intended recipient or beneficiary in many common contexts.
Use para for many deadlines or target times.
